skill.description: Query NCBI ClinVar for variant clinical significance, review status, API access, FTP data formats, and VCF annotation workflows.

skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The skill is a documentation-heavy ClinVar reference with many scanner hits from Markdown examples, public NCBI URLs, and inline code spans. Most static findings are false positives, but the FTP-based remote installer command is a real high-risk pattern and FTP dataset downloads carry medium transport-integrity risk.

remediation.issue: Remote installer command executes a script fetched over FTP.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the shell-piped installer example or replace it with a link to official instructions, HTTPS transport, and checksum verification.

remediation.issue: Bulk download examples use FTP URLs without integrity verification.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer HTTPS endpoints when available and document checksum or signature verification before processing downloaded files.

remediation.issue: Command examples could be auto-executed by an agent without user review.
remediation.suggestion: State that shell commands are examples only and require explicit user approval before execution.

remediation.issue: API key guidance places the key in a URL query parameter.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that users must protect API keys, avoid logging full request URLs, and avoid storing keys in prompts.

content.value_statement: ClinVar data is large, versioned, and difficult to query safely. This skill guides targeted searches, API retrieval, format selection, and clinical significance interpretation.
actual_capabilities: Search ClinVar by gene, condition, variant name, chromosome, and clinical significance.
Explain pathogenicity terms, VUS handling, review status ratings, and conflicting interpretations.
Use NCBI E-utilities examples for esearch, esummary, efetch, and elink workflows.
Choose between XML, VCF, and tab-delimited ClinVar data formats for analysis tasks.
Plan VCF annotation and filtering workflows with ClinVar clinical significance fields.
Summarize ClinVar update schedules, submission routes, and reproducibility considerations.
limitations: It does not replace review by a genetics professional or clinical laboratory.
ClinVar classifications can change as submissions and evidence are updated.
It provides guidance, but it does not execute API queries or downloads by itself.
VCF guidance excludes some large or complex variants that are not represented in VCF files.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Gene Variants
use_cases.description: Find pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants for a gene and rank them by review status.

use_cases.title: Annotate Sequencing Results
use_cases.description: Select ClinVar files and fields for adding clinical significance annotations to a VCF.

use_cases.title: Build Reproducible Data Pulls
use_cases.description: Plan API or bulk-data retrieval with version tracking, rate limits, and format selection.

prompt_templates.title: Find Variants by Gene
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ClinVar skill to explain how I can search for pathogenic BRCA1 variants. Include web and E-utilities options.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Review Confidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ClinVar review status guidance to compare variants in BRCA2. Explain which ratings need manual review before use.

prompt_templates.title: Plan VCF Annotation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a workflow to annotate a GRCh38 VCF with ClinVar clinical significance. Include file choice, filters, and reproducibility notes.

prompt_templates.title: Design Local Refresh Process
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a local ClinVar database refresh process using XML, VCF, and tab-delimited releases. Include version tracking and validation checks.

output_examples.input: Explain what a ClinVar VUS result means for a researcher.
output_examples.output: The variant has uncertain significance. It should not be treated as disease-causing without more evidence and expert review.

output_examples.input: Choose a format for annotating a sequencing VCF.
output: Use the ClinVar VCF that matches the genome build.
Track the ClinVar release date for reproducibility.
Flag conflicting or low-review classifications for manual review.

output_examples.input: Summarize a safe ClinVar query plan for TP53.
output_examples.output: Start with a web query, confirm search terms, then use E-utilities with rate limits and cached results.

best_practices: Always record the ClinVar release date, genome build, and access method used for analysis.
Prioritize expert panel or practice guideline review status when interpreting clinical significance.
Treat conflicting interpretations, VUS results, and low-review variants as requiring manual review.
anti_patterns: Do not use ClinVar output as a standalone clinical diagnosis.
Do not mix GRCh37 and GRCh38 files without explicit coordinate handling.
Do not automate large API or FTP pulls without rate limits, caching, and integrity checks.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps query ClinVar, interpret clinical significance fields, and choose data formats for variant analysis.

faq.question: Can it make clinical decisions?
faq.answer: No. ClinVar evidence must be reviewed by qualified genetics professionals before clinical use.

faq.question: Which data formats does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers XML, VCF, and tab-delimited ClinVar files, including common strengths and limitations.

faq.question: Does it support API workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents NCBI E-utilities workflows for searching, summarizing, fetching, and linking records.

faq.question: How should I handle conflicting interpretations?
faq.answer: Review star ratings, submitter evidence, dates, and expert panel classifications before drawing conclusions.

faq.question: What should I track for reproducibility?
faq.answer: Track the ClinVar release, access date, genome build, query terms, and filters used in the workflow.
